conviction_note: No unpriced company-level number found. Q3 should land inside or at the top of a $210-220M guide that consensus already sits in. The reaction turns on the Q4 guide and a third raise to the 2026 optical outlook. The market will expect that raise, because the last raise of more than $50M was sold for -21.5%, and supply tightness and the 1.6T timing cap the upside. The stock has already de-rated 49% from its high, -14% today on sector selling with no company news, which lowers the bar. Net is a slight negative lean (p_up 47) on a large unsigned move (13%, the name's median reaction; the 7.06% option event figure is understated because ordinary vol of 116% is subtracted). impact_sum -1.7 is about twice the scaled number because the findings are small and lean negative, and the pre-print flush is the one item that cuts the other way.

findings.finding: Q3 revenue is guided at $210-220M (+27% q/q from $168.8M) and consensus sits at $210-215M, low-to-mid of the guide. MXL beat revenue estimates about 88% of the time over two years, and Q2 printed $168.8M against a $160-170M guide, in the upper half, so a print near $218-220M (about +2-3% over the bar) is likely. It lands inside the guided range.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: revenue $168.8M beat the $164.6M consensus and EPS beat by $0.02; the stock fell 21.54%. Q1 2026: revenue beat with a big optical raise; +76%. Q4 2025 and Q3 2025 beats: -10.0% and -10.8%. Revenue beats inside the guide have been sold.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: consensus already sits inside the guide. The only unpriced part is the upper-half landing ($218-220M against a $210-215M consensus). If the market had priced it, consensus would sit at the top of the guide.
findings.independence: Beat-rate statistic from GuruFocus 2026-10-21 (https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9135267/maxlinear-mxl-set-to-report-q3-earnings-amid-elevated-pricetosales-valuation). Shares the guide document with finding 2.

findings.finding: The 2026 optical data center outlook has been raised twice: at Q1 to $150-170M, and at Q2 to $210-230M (more than $50M higher, all from Keystone 800G). The Investing.com preview says the company has 'raised its full-year optical outlook multiple times' and an analyst calls 'December conversion the primary test'. A third raise is the market's bar, and a reaffirmation would read as deceleration.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The first optical raise (Q1, to $150-170M) bought +76%. The second raise (Q2, +$50M to $210-230M) was sold: +5% on the print day, then -9.6% after hours and -21.54% over the window.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the 49% de-rating from the high says the market has cut how much raise it pays for. If a third raise were fully priced, the stock would not have sold the second one. If a reaffirmation were priced, the stock would not still trade at 12x sales (GuruFocus) with seven of 11 analysts at Buy and a $95 consensus target.
findings.independence: Q1 raise to $150-170M from Q1 call coverage (https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/04/24/why-maxlinear-stock-soared-more-than-80-today/). Preview language from https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/maxlinear-earnings-set-to-test-optical-surge-and-16t-shift-93CH-4966536 (2026-10-22).

findings.finding: On the Q2 call management said supply is tight, wafer prepayments are rising, and wafer/packaging/test input costs are going up and only partly passed on. Q3 non-GAAP GM is guided at 58.5-61.5% (mid 60%) against 59.5% in Q2, and the preview flags whether mix offsets rising wafer and packaging costs. Supply caps how far Q4 can be guided above Q3, and GM is at risk of landing at or below the guide midpoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history of a GM surprise for this name. Q2 GM of 59.5% was in line and the stock fell on the forward read.
findings.why_not_priced: The margin guide is public. What is not priced is whether supply limits the Q4 revenue step. If it were priced, EPS estimates would have risen with revenue; instead they were flat over 60 days while revenue rose 2.2% (Investing.com preview).
findings.independence: The preview's GM focus and the flat EPS revisions: https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/maxlinear-earnings-set-to-test-optical-surge-and-16t-shift-93CH-4966536. Shares the Q2 transcript with finding 2.

findings.finding: MXL fell to $65.36 intraday on 2026-10-22, about -14% from the $75.79 close of 10-21 (-23% over 20d, -49% from the $128.30 high), in a sector-wide sell-off with no company news. Optics peers fell 9-12% (Coherent -12%, AAOI -10%, Lumentum -9%, LYTE ETF -10%; LSCC -10.4%, SMTC -12.1%), and MXL has filed no 8-K since 2026-07-23. The bar for the print is reset lower before the window opens at today's close.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The opposite setup last time: Q2 2026 rose 5% on the print day into the release and then fell 21.5%. No record of a pre-print flush on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: The sell-off is visible, so this is a statement about the bar and not hidden information. The open question is whether a sector move that was not about MXL resets expectations below what the print delivers. If the market saw it as an over-reaction, the drop would not have deepened into the afternoon. Sector momentum can just as easily carry into 10-23, which is why it is sized small.
findings.independence: Alphastreet 2026-10-22: MXL -10.3% with peers falling (https://news.alphastreet.com/maxlinear-plunges-10-3-amid-sector-wide-selling/). EDGAR filing list: no 8-K since 2026-07-23 (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001288469&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40).

findings.finding: The 10-Q (per Zacks) shows inventory-purchase and other contractual obligations rising to $305.9M from $209.6M at 2025-12-31, inventory up to $105.5M (6/30) from $85.8M (3/31), and wafer prepayments rising (H1 operating cash flow -$4.1M). Against roughly $85M of quarterly COGS this is about 3.5 quarters of committed supply. The cash is buying capacity for a ramp, which corroborates a Q4 step-up rather than signalling distress.
findings.why_not_priced: The commitments are in the 10-Q but previews read cash burn and inventory as a risk, not as forward volume. If they were priced as a ramp, Q4 numbers would be explicit in previews; no source carried a Q4 revenue consensus.
findings.independence: Q2 call: purchase obligations rose about $40M on prepayments, and days of inventory fell to 123 from 128, so inventory is turning faster, not piling up (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-maxlinear-beats-q2-2026-estimates-then-falls-after-hours-93CH-4810148).

findings.finding: Broadband (about $45M, 27% of Q2 revenue) faces a memory-cost squeeze on CPE. Counterpoint puts consumer memory for routers/STBs up about 7x, with memory now more than 20% of router BOM, and warns of slower deployments. Realtek's Q2 GM fell 2.7 points on memory costs. Management nonetheless guided growth in all four segments for Q3 and cited PON share gains.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolated; broadband is no longer the line the stock trades on.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a proxy, macro-to-company, and not confirmed by MXL or a direct customer. The rest of the company matters more: infrastructure is about 50% and growing triple digits, so even a soft broadband quarter is a few $M against a $215M bar.
findings.independence: Realtek Q2 2026 GM fell on memory costs (https://quartr.com/events/realtek-semiconductor-corp-2379-q2-2026_F91HVnhJ). Proxy only.

findings.finding: Peers that reported after MXL last spoke show 800G/1.6T optical demand still accelerating. Credo's FQ1 (ended Aug 1) revenue was $479M against a $465-475M guide, with record optical DSP revenue, an FQ2 guide of $525-535M and an optical target above $600M for FY27. Innolight's H1 2026 revenue was +182% and Eoptolink's +100%. This supports Keystone volumes into Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Industry demand was strong into Q2 too, and the stock still fell 21.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: These are industry proxies the market has seen. Credo is also a competing optical DSP vendor ramping into the same sockets, so strong peer numbers do not automatically mean share for MXL.
findings.independence: Innolight H1 2026 (https://stockanalysis.com/quote/she/300308/revenue/), Eoptolink H1 2026 (https://filingreader.com/news-wire/shenzhen/2026-07-19/eoptolink-net-profit-to-double-on-ai-computing-demand). Both are proxies.

findings.finding: MXL's 1.6T DSP (Rushmore) earns first revenue only in 2027, with a 2H27 ramp at one or two customers and bigger ramps in 2028-29. Industry leader Innolight already has 1.6T modules in volume ramp in 2026, and Credo targets 1.6T DSP revenue in FY27. The previews frame the print around the '1.6T shift'. MXL's growth into 2027 rests on 800G Keystone while the market migrates, so Q4 and 2027 commentary risks reading as an 800G peak.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: questions about growth durability beyond the current ramps accompanied a -21.5% reaction to a beat-and-raise.
findings.why_not_priced: This is an inference. Previews frame 1.6T as an opportunity (Samsung foundry advantage, about 2x pricing) rather than as a gap. If the market priced the gap, the consensus target would not be $95 against a $65 stock. It is partly priced through the de-rating.
findings.independence: Innolight's 1.6T volume ramp (https://stockanalysis.com/quote/she/300308/revenue/ via the H1 summary) and the Investing.com preview's 1.6T framing (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/maxlinear-earnings-set-to-test-optical-surge-and-16t-shift-93CH-4966536). Shares the Q2 transcript with findings 2 and 3.

findings.finding: The 10-Q (per Zacks) discloses that one customer was 11% of H1 2026 revenue and the top 10 were 55%, while management said on the Q2 call that no customer exceeds 10%. Concentration is rising into hyperscaler/module ramps, which management itself said will increase.
findings.why_not_priced: Small and public. The 11% may be a distributor, which would reconcile it with the call. It matters only if Q3 shows a single optical customer pause.
findings.independence: Q2 call statement 'no customer over 10%' (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-maxlinear-beats-q2-2026-estimates-then-falls-after-hours-93CH-4810148). Shares the Zacks article with finding 7.

baseline_tension: The findings lean slightly negative, in line with the modest downside skew (+3.8) and the name's habit of selling beats (5 of 7 reactions down). They cut against the 49% de-rating and today's -14% sector flush, which have already lowered the bar, so p_up sits only 3 points below 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 / rule 6 (inside the guide, beats sold): the Q3 beat finding cut from +0.5 to +0.2 because it lands inside the $210-220M guide and this name sold its last beats.

Rule 5 (drawdown is not a cause; proxy sizing): the pre-print sector flush cut from +1.0 to +0.5. The cause is sourced (sector selling), but mean reversion of a drawdown is an inference, not a company document.
Rule 5 (proxies smaller): peer demand cut from +0.5 to +0.3 and the broadband memory squeeze from -0.3 to -0.2. Both are kept as filed proxies.

Rule 4 (financing is a question): purchase obligations and prepayments signed positive as ramp corroboration and trimmed from +0.5 to +0.4, since days of inventory fell and nothing indicates distress.
Rule 3 (caveat reaches the number): the 1.6T timing finding cut from -0.8 to -0.6 because its own text notes previews frame 1.6T as an opportunity.
Rule 7: short interest was looked up before the negatives (5.4%, 1.5 days, not crowded) and the skew is modest, so no shrink for squeeze risk.
